title: Grateful Dead Live at St. Paul Auditorium on 1973-02-17
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat -> CD  D

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1973 show with standout Here Comes Sunshine → China > I Know You Rider and solid soundboard mix despite occasional tape glitches
ai_review.review: The February 17 1973 St. Paul concert delivers a lively setlist that mixes new material (TLEO, He's Gone) with classics, highlighted by a smoking Here Comes Sunshine/China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider sequence and an inspired Row Jimmy. Charlie Miller’s soundboard mix is generally clear and well‑balanced, though listeners note some tape cuts and on‑stage sound hiccups in the first set.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4–5 stars, praising performance and mix; only a few note minor technical flaws, yielding an overall strong positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp Charlie Miller mix with occasional tape cuts, on‑stage sound issues and brief distortion during louder moments; otherwise clear and well balanced.

standout_songs: Here Comes Sunshine > China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Loose Lucy (needs more work per some listeners)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A well‑curated mix of new 1973 material and older favorites; smooth transitions especially the sunshine/China > Rider segue, with a strong second‑set that builds energy toward a classic encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Soulful, lilting guitar work; great tone noted throughout, standout vocals on Looks Like Rain and He's Gone, plus his whah‑whah petal on GDTRFB.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass "bombs" – especially brilliant during the Playin' in the Band segment; consistently exceptional throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Strong vocal delivery on Looks Like Rain and Bobby McGee; adds energy to the performance.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's rag‑time piano shines on Looks Like Rain and supports the band with melodic fills across the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy Kreutzmann’s drumming praised (Beer Barrel Polka), Mickey Hart also noted for solid backbeat.
